hypotheses.proposition: Selected Canadian household-security and per-capita trajectory changes preceded directionally comparable U.S. changes by approximately six years.
required_evidence: Reviewed national structural-break findings by aligned indicator
disconfirming_conditions: U.S. precedes Canada on material indicators

hypotheses.proposition: Both countries can display aggregate economic strength while economic security deteriorates for material household groups.
required_evidence: Reviewed median and distributional household findings
disconfirming_conditions: Household security broadly improves with aggregate measures
Apparent divergence is caused by incompatible definitions or temporary revisions

hypotheses.proposition: The tariff-target and tariff-imposing countries experience overlapping losses in efficiency, investment, employment, or household purchasing power through different domestic mechanisms.
required_evidence: Reviewed Canadian export-shock and diversification effects
Reviewed U.S. importer downstream and household incidence
disconfirming_conditions: Measured benefits dominate costs in one country across the declared horizon
Effects are confined to non-comparable sectors or periods

hypotheses.proposition: Canada may exchange short-run efficiency for diversified resilience while the United States may exchange efficiency for domestic productive capacity, with neither strategic result guaranteed.
required_evidence: Canadian product-level diversification durability and margins
U.S. competitive capacity investment and productivity
Long-run consumer producer worker and fiscal effects
disconfirming_conditions: Diversification is temporary rerouting without durable buyers
Protected U.S. output does not create competitive capacity
